### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`, touching **4** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via ApprovalService (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via ApprovalService (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **6** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a57643d3de7067cb7d292b4802773bdf938fd2cb` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `df7d5c84c171734a3ae467cbaa84aa234a95984c` — the merge of head `d7a204a5150c743ee4dec70f80783384444dc3b7` into base `a57643d3de7067cb7d292b4802773bdf938fd2cb`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin df7d5c84c171734a3ae467cbaa84aa234a95984c && git checkout df7d5c84c171734a3ae467cbaa84aa234a95984c
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin a57643d3de7067cb7d292b4802773bdf938fd2cb d7a204a5150c743ee4dec70f80783384444dc3b7 && git checkout -B drift-repro a57643d3de7067cb7d292b4802773bdf938fd2cb && git merge --no-ff d7a204a5150c743ee4dec70f80783384444dc3b7

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a57643d3de7067cb7d292b4802773bdf938fd2cb
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs a57643d3de7067cb7d292b4802773bdf938fd2cb` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `d7a204a5150c743ee4dec70f80783384444dc3b7`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/approval-sla-reassign-target-resolves.dogfood.test.ts, .changeset/25598-sla-reassign-target-resolves.md + packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts (`notify`, `expandPositionUsers`, `reassign`, `assertReassignTargetResolves` docblock, `runEscalations`, `slateLabels`, `approverRequestIds`), packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approver-address.ts (`addressedPosition`), packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/translations/messages.ts (`approvalSlaBreachedSubmitterBody`), packages/spec/src/automation/approval.zod.ts (`ApprovalEscalationSchema.escalateTo`), packages/spec/src/automation/flow-node-config-refusals.ts (the `approval` contract row), packages/qa/dogfood/test/fixtures/admin-rescue-slate-fixture.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/approval-admin-rescue-slate.dogfood.test.ts and approval-reassign-target-resolves.dogfood.test.ts (the `approverId` list form), packages/services/service-messaging/src/messaging-service.ts (`source_id`), packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-service.ts (the #25591 text), .github/workflows/ci.yml (the dogfood `pull_request` skip)

Inputs: card #25598 body and both comments (claim 6379436604, spec-lane pointer 6379444004); PR #25600 body, file list and the net diff `a57643d3..d7a204a5` (4 files, +392/-23, one commit; the tree of `d7a204a5` is `bfa5e7fb`, identical to the tree of the `4525d322` the Verification section names); the 42 check-runs on the head: every gate-carrying run `success`, the dogfood shards, Verify CLI, Console Pin Gate, Temporal Conformance and the two opt-in harnesses `skipped` on `pull_request` by design (ci.yml `if:` on the dogfood matrix). Read-only: nothing built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

**Accept set: unchanged — `Clause-②: no` with no arm is right.** Nothing the diff touches registers or refuses metadata: `packages/spec` is untouched, `ApprovalEscalationSchema.escalateTo` stays `z.string().optional()`, `flow-node-config-refusals.ts` still judges the `approval` node whole against `ApprovalNodeConfigSchema` and no new check is added to it. The REST door's refusal is byte-identical to #25592's: `assertReassignTargetResolves` became a throw over `reassignTargetRefusal`, whose branches and sentences are the old ones moved, so no door narrows. Nothing widens either: no new accepted value, no new export (both methods are `private`), no new error code, no route change. What moves is the runtime outcome of one path, an overdue request whose `reassign` target names no one, and that path was a defect (the request left on a slate nobody could decide, the state #25485 closed for the door), not a contract an author could rely on. A `(narrowing)` arm would claim a refusal that does not exist; its absence is right.

**Reusing the door predicate for `escalateTo`'s bare-name / user-id contract: sound.** The order of judgment preserves the published contract ("user id or position machine name"): the sweep still tries the bare value as a position first (`expandPositionUsers` over `sys_user_position` plus the membership-tier source, organization-scoped); only an EMPTY expansion reaches the predicate, and the predicate then reads the bare value as the door does: `position:` plus a name resolves through `addressedPosition` to holders in the request's organization; any other `type:value` literal is refused outright (no actor acts under `team:` / `department:` / `org_membership_level:` / stored `role:`, per approver-address.ts); a bare value is a `sys_user` id or, with an `@`, an email, then the "not provably a member of other organizations only" membership test. So a staffed position name never reaches the predicate, a user id with an account still reassigns, and both callers yield the same five outcomes. Two postures ride in from the door unchanged and are the door's stated contract, not new: an email is matched as stored (case-exact, the spelling a default actor takes a slot under), and an unreadable `sys_member` reads as no tenancy fact (resolves). The predicate's own `expandPositionUsers` swallows a failed `sys_user_position` read as "no holder" inside it, again as the door does.

**Submitter notice reporting the action TAKEN: right.** The template is a statement of fact ("escalation action 'ACTION' was taken", four locales), and it was false whenever `reassign` fell to the notify branch, both in the new unresolved case and in the pre-existing no-`escalateTo` case; `taken` fixes both. The configured action is not lost: the `escalate` audit row still leads with it (`reassign → target`) and gains the `not applied: why` suffix only when the slate was kept, so the row distinguishes a reassign that happened from one that was declined. In the unresolved case the `approval.sla_breached` audience is the pending slate only (`escalatees` cleared), which is right: the literal names no one to tell, and `notify` would drop a `type:value` address anyway.

**Failed `sys_user` read: throw before the audit row is right.** The predicate's `sys_user` read is outside any `catch`, so it propagates out of `escalateRequest` before the `sys_approval_action` insert; nothing is written, `runEscalations`' per-request `try` logs at `warn` and continues to the next row; the next sweep finds no `escalate` row and retries. ADR-0042 §1 (the row is the marker, written before any mutation) is honoured because no mutation happened. `warn` is the right level under AGENTS.md's one question: nothing claims to be persisted, the system is visibly behind (the request is still overdue and pending) and a retry is scheduled. The cost is one warn per overdue reassign request per sweep while the directory is down; no durability is at stake.

**Tests.** The two edits to existing fixtures (`staffDirectory(engine, 'boss')`) make a precondition explicit that the predicate now enforces; the PR names both. The new block pins, per refusal case, the slate CSV, the labels, the approver index, the audit sentence verbatim, both audiences, the submitter's `'notify'`, the absence of `approval.escalated`, and a second sweep as a no-op; the failed-read case pins no row, no notice, and the retry; the preservation case pins id, email and `position:` plus a held name, with the holder deciding as the default actor. The dogfood pin boots the real composition, drives the sweep through the registered `approvals` service, and uses two shapes already in service: the `approverId=id,email` list form that `approval-admin-rescue-slate` and `approval-reassign-target-resolves` use, and `sys_notification.source_id`, which messaging-service writes from `source.id`. Because the dogfood matrix is skipped on `pull_request`, this pin's first CI execution is on `main`'s full battery after merge; until then the author's local battery (new pin green) is the only evidence, which is the repo's design for dogfood pins, not a gap in this PR.

**Two observations, neither blocking.** (a) The spec's `escalateTo` description names "user id or position machine name" and not the `position:` plus name and email spellings the runtime (door and sweep alike) judges; the spec-lane seat taking the registration leg should read it. (b) `notify` drops `type:value` audiences, so a reassign to a held `position:` literal announces itself to no one; pre-existing, pinned as it is today, and not a strand (the holder finds the request through the index fold and can decide it).

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/plugin-approvals: patch` is right: a bug fix in a released package, kind `none`. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right: no key, accepted value or type is added or removed, the key's published text and default are unchanged, and the outcome that changes is for a value outside the key's stated contract (one naming neither a position nor a user). `Clause-②: no` with no arm, as judged above; both declaration lines are identical in the PR body and the changeset body. No BREAKING banner and no ADR-0087 marker is right: there is no `(narrowing)` arm, no removal, no rename, no alias. `Check Changeset` is green on the head. The changeset's body carries no tracker number in its prose beyond the filename, and its last line tells an author what to write to make a timeout move.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **`Refs #25598`, not `Fixes`: answered, right.** The card has two legs; this PR lands the runtime leg the claim 6379436604 scoped, and the card stays open for the registration leg. `Part-of PR must not also close its card` and `The card this PR closes must claim this branch` are both green.
- **The registration leg left to the spec lane: answered, right placement; one escalation.** An approval node's `escalation` is judged at registration by `ApprovalNodeConfigSchema` through `flow-node-config-refusals.ts` (the `approval` row of the declared plugin contracts), so refusing a `team:` / `department:` / `org_membership_level:` / `role:` literal there is a `packages/spec` edit, which the `domain:server` seat does not make. Escalation: as of this read the card carries the services seat's pointer (6379444004) and no claim from a `domain:spec` seat, so the second leg is unowned. Not this PR's defect; the coordinator should see it routed.
- **The dogfood battery failure attributed to #25591: verified, and it carries a landing constraint.** `main`'s push runs at `4a251927` (#25591) and at `a57643d3` (the merge base, before this PR) both conclude `failure`; on the merge-base run the only non-green jobs are `Dogfood Regression Gate (1/3)` and its aggregate. The sentence the failing pin now receives is the one `sharing-service.ts` carries at `main` lines 1419-1424 since #25591, and this diff touches no sharing path. The red is filed as card #25602 (04:35Z, `domain:server`, p1, dispatched). Escalation to the owning seat: #25602 sits on the same lane as this PR, and Multi-agent discipline §7 says no lane PR arms the queue while a full-battery main-red is the lane's first work, so this PR's arming waits for #25602's fix to land (or for the lane to rule the red belongs elsewhere). The verdict on the diff is unaffected.
- **Email matched as stored (case-exact) in the predicate:** inherited from #25592's door, stated in its docblock, now applied consistently to the sweep; noted, no action.
- **The `notify` drop of `type:value` audiences:** the PR's own note; answered above as a pre-existing functional gap, not a strand, pinned as today's behaviour.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-h5z02d`
Reviewed-by: `session_01HopxxRtFE6z3z91wUD54tp`

**VERDICT: PASS**
